results.title: 2.5M views · 108K reactions | “Formatting issues” is a ridiculously insulting excuse. But this isn’t just about fake citations. It’s about what happens when you dismantle the institutions that protect public health and replace them with something that looks scientific, but isn’t. It’s performing science without actually doing it. All while undermining the very systems that make real scientific inquiry and public health possible. This is how authoritarian health regimes take shape. By flooding the zone with junk “science” and false equivalencies that erode trust and confuse the public until no one knows what’s real. These were not formatting issues. Let’s not let this administration insult our intelligence and gaslight us like that. This was dishonest and a blatant disregard for basic research standards. It would’ve earned a failing grade in a university science course. And it’s a failure here, too. | Jessica Knurick, PhD, RD

I can’t fathom how you can keep up this pace of output, but I always look forward to your posts. The central contradiction of the MAHA movement is that many of the goals people say they want, including stronger regulation of food additives, tighter oversight of pesticides and environmental toxins, and more accountability for pharmaceutical and food corporations, fundamentally require government regulation and strong public health agencies. When the synthetic form of a vitamin is chemically identical to the one found in food, your body uses it the same way. What matters for variability is the form, not whether it came from a lemon or a lab.
